title: Agent Definition
description: A platform-agnostic, harness-agnostic JSON document from which an agent harness can configure a functional subagent. See Agents/agent-definition/README.md for the normative prose specification. Vendor- or implementation-specific data belongs in the spec-defined `extensions` object, not in invented top-level fields.

spec_version.description: The version of the Agent Definition specification that this document conforms to, as SemVer 2.0.0.

model.description: An ordered list of model preferences, most preferred first. A harness MUST attempt entries in order and use the first it can satisfy, or map it to its nearest equivalent and report the substitution.

bootstrap.description: A single text blob of bootstrap context for the agent (role, domain knowledge, procedures, rules). The spec defines no internal structure for this text; a harness MUST treat it as opaque, untrusted natural-language content.

skills.description: References to published, maintained skills the agent may use. Never embedded.

tools.description: References to published, maintained tools (including MCP servers) the agent may use. Never embedded.

allOf.description: Validity rule 1 (inclusive anyOf, NOT oneOf): at least one of metadata.name or metadata.role MUST be present. Both MAY be present.
Validity rule 2 (inclusive anyOf, NOT oneOf): at least one substantive field MUST be present. Any combination of these fields MAY be present.

metadata.description: Descriptive information about this agent definition. At least one of name or role is REQUIRED (enforced at the document level, not here, so that this sub-schema stays reusable).

id.description: An opaque, globally-unique identifier for this agent definition (e.g. a reverse-DNS string or UUID). Distinct from identity; this identifies the DOCUMENT, not a persona.

name.description: The agent's display/invocation name (e.g. "Scout"). SHOULD be present when identity is present.

role.description: A human-readable description of what the agent does (e.g. "Research", "Quality Assurance"), used by harnesses to derive a fallback handle when name is absent.

version.description: The version of this particular agent definition (not of the spec), as SemVer.

description.description: A longer, free-text description of the agent for humans browsing a registry or catalog.

license.description: An SPDX license identifier for this agent definition document.

modelPreference.description: One entry in the ordered model preference list. provider and model are the core sub-fields and are REQUIRED. settings is a free-form object whose keys and values are that provider's OWN parameter names (e.g. Anthropic's thinking object, OpenAI's reasoning_effort, Google's thinkingConfig). The spec defines no global reasoning/thinking vocabulary.

provider.description: An identifier for the model provider (e.g. "anthropic", "openai", "google"). Not constrained to an enum so new providers need no spec change.

model.description: The provider's own model identifier string (e.g. "claude-sonnet-4-5", "gpt-5").

label.description: An optional human-readable label for this preference entry.

settings.description: Provider- and model-specific parameters, using that provider's own parameter names and value shapes (e.g. reasoning/thinking effort or budget). Opaque to this spec.

identity.description: WHO the agent is: name, persona, voice, values, pronouns. Composed before bootstrap. Separate from bootstrap so a harness with its own identity can use, replace, or ignore it per a declared policy.

persona.description: The core identity text: who the agent is, in the agent's own voice or a description of it. Core sub-field; REQUIRED whenever identity is present.

voice.description: Free-text description of tone, register, and speaking style.

locator.description: Shared locator shape for skill and tool references: a registry id or a URL (or both), optionally pinned to a version or version range, optionally integrity-checked.

id.description: A registry identifier for the referenced skill, tool, or MCP server.

url.description: A URL locating the referenced skill, tool, or MCP server (e.g. its manifest, package, or connection endpoint).

version.description: An exact version of the referenced skill or tool.

version_range.description: A version range/constraint for the referenced skill or tool (e.g. "^1.2.0", "~3.1"), in whatever range syntax the registry uses.

name.description: An optional human-readable label for this skill reference.

toolReference.description: A reference to a tool or an MCP server. required marks whether the agent needs this tool to function: if a harness cannot satisfy a reference with required = true, it MUST refuse to instantiate the agent rather than run a degraded agent.

required.description: Whether this tool is required for the agent to function. If true and the harness cannot satisfy it, the harness MUST refuse to instantiate the agent.

kind.description: The kind of reference. "mcp_server" indicates the locator points at an MCP server (by registry id or connection URL) rather than a single tool.

name.description: An optional human-readable label for this tool reference.

permissions.description: Declared operating limits for the agent. The harness MUST enforce what it can and MUST report what it cannot enforce. At least one sub-field is REQUIRED once this block is present.

side_effects.description: A declared list of side-effect classes this agent may perform (e.g. "sends_notifications", "spends_funds"). Free-form strings; the spec defines no global enum.

contract.description: An I/O contract for the agent, expressed as JSON Schemas. At least one of input or output is REQUIRED once this block is present.

input.description: A JSON Schema describing the agent's expected input.

output.description: A JSON Schema describing the agent's produced output.

integrity.description: A content hash over this document (or the referenced artifact), computed over the JSON canonicalized per RFC 8785 (JCS). algorithm and value are the core sub-fields and are REQUIRED once this block is present.

value.description: The hash digest, hex- or base64-encoded.

canonicalization.description: The canonicalization scheme the hash was computed over. This spec defines RFC 8785 (JCS) as the canonicalization scheme for agent definitions.

extensions.description: A free-form, spec-defined extension point for vendor- or implementation-specific data that does not require a spec update. Keys SHOULD be namespaced (reverse-DNS or a short vendor prefix, e.g. "org.example.harness") to avoid collisions. Values MAY be any JSON. A harness MUST ignore namespaces it does not understand and MUST NOT refuse to instantiate because of unknown extension content. A harness SHOULD preserve this object unchanged when it re-exports or transforms a definition. Extensions MUST NOT override the meaning of any spec-defined field.
